meta.label: Admin Toolkit
meta.description: Dataiku DSS administration toolkit: diagnostics, visualizations, and management tools, with multi-instance scanning across remote DSS hosts.
meta.author: Alex Kaos

params.name: sep_security
params.label: Advanced Actions
params.description: Create your secret on the secret generator — type a password there, then paste the result below.

params.name: red_actions_secret
params.label: Advanced Actions secret
params.description: Paste the secret from the link above to enable advanced actions (delete / replace / migrate / deploy / send). Leave empty to keep them locked.

params.name: dbhealth_connection
params.label: RuntimeDB Connection
params.description: PostgreSQL connection for DB Health tool (typically 'runtimedb'). Select (None) to disable DB Health.

params.name: dataset_export_connection
params.label: Target Connection
params.description: Connection used to store UI tables saved as managed datasets (into the Admin Toolkit webapp's own project). Select (None) to disable the toolbar button.

params.name: sep_archive
params.label: Archive Storage
params.description: Where the toolkit stores backup artifacts: deleted code envs and deleted projects (cleaner backups), and 'Export all' zips.

params.name: archive_folder_connection
params.label: Archive Folders Connection
params.description: Connection on which the toolkit auto-creates its 'admin-toolkit-archive' managed folder (default destination for cleaner backups and export zips). Select (None) to keep picking existing folders manually.

params.name: outreach_mail_channel
params.label: Mail Channel ID
params.description: DSS messaging channel ID used for outreach emails (e.g. 'mail-channel-1'). Leave empty to auto-select the first available channel.

params.name: sep_agents_audit
params.label: Agents Audit Database
params.description: PostgreSQL connection holding the agents audit trail (agents.agent_actions), written by the agents plugin and shown in the Agents audit timeline.

params.name: agents_audit_postgres_connection
params.label: Agents Audit PostgreSQL Connection
params.description: PostgreSQL connection (on this hub) where the agents plugin records its audit trail. Select (None) if the agents plugin is not in use.

params.name: sep_chat_persistence
params.label: Agents — Chat persistence
params.description: Optionally persist webapp agent conversations server-side (per user, per fleet host). Off = browser-only, as before. Built-in = SQLite in the webapp's workload folder. Remote SQL = a PostgreSQL or SQL Server DSS connection. Storage changes apply on the next webapp backend restart.

params.name: chat_db_connection
params.label: Chat SQL connection
params.description: PostgreSQL or SQL Server connection where conversations are stored. The webapp backend reads the connection details, so it needs details-readability on this connection.

params.name: chat_tables_prefix
params.label: Chat tables prefix
params.description: Physical table-name prefix (lowercase letters, digits, underscores).

params.name: backend_url
params.label: Backend base URL
params.description: Admin Toolkit webapp backend base, e.g. https://dss.example.com/web-apps-backends/PROJECT/webappId — leave empty to auto-discover the webapp on the local DSS.

params.name: red_actions_password
params.label: Advanced Actions password
params.description: Plaintext Advanced Actions password (used to unlock red endpoints headlessly). Leave empty to keep all mutating actions permanently locked.

params.name: host_keys_password
params.label: Remote host keys password
params.description: Password for encrypted remote-host API keys (adkfk1$ blobs). Leave empty if no remote host uses an encrypted key.

params.name: host_allowlist
params.label: Host allowlist
params.description: Comma-separated host ids agents may target (from the toolkit's host list). Empty = all configured hosts.

params.name: http_timeout_s
params.label: HTTP timeout (s)
params.description: Timeout for normal backend endpoints.

params.name: heavy_timeout_s
params.label: Heavy-scan timeout (s)
params.description: Timeout for heavy scan endpoints (code envs, project footprint, CRU). On timeout, tools report scan_running with re-invoke advice.

params.name: default_llm_id
params.label: Default LLM
params.description: LLM Mesh model used by the plugin agents unless overridden per agent.

params.name: enable_red_actions
params.label: Enable red actions
params.description: Master kill-switch. OFF = execute-admin-action always refuses, regardless of per-agent settings.

params.name: triage_connection
params.label: Triage PostgreSQL connection
params.description: Postgres connection where daily triage results and the agent-action audit trail persist (same connection as the toolkit's Agents Audit setting). (None) disables the triage loop.

params.name: triage_score_threshold
params.label: Triage score threshold
params.description: Hosts scoring below this get an LLM-drafted recommendation in the daily sweep.

params.name: sep_auto_remediate
params.label: Agents — Auto-remediation
params.description: Actions listed below run AUTONOMOUSLY during the daily triage sweep when their finding fires — no per-run human approval. Listing an action here is the admin's standing approval for that action, within the caps; everything else stays plan → approve → execute. The enable_red_actions kill-switch still gates every run, and every run is audited (agent='triage-auto') and reported in the digest.

params.name: auto_remediate_actions
params.label: Auto-remediate actions (CSV)
params.description: Comma-separated action names the triage loop may execute autonomously. Only reversible capped cleanups are eligible: log-cleanup, docker-prune. Empty = tier off (the digest still reports what WOULD have run).

params.name: auto_remediate_max_gb
params.label: Auto-remediate cap (GB per sweep)
params.description: Cumulative reclaim cap across all autonomous fixes in one sweep.

params.name: auto_remediate_max_objects
params.label: Auto-remediate cap (objects per sweep)
params.description: Cumulative deleted-object cap across all autonomous fixes in one sweep.

params.name: log_cleanup_min_age_days
params.label: Log cleanup minimum age (days)
params.description: Rotated logs younger than this are never deleted (applies to agent-planned and autonomous log-cleanup).

params.name: settings_set_blocked_extra
params.label: Extra blocked settings paths (CSV)
params.description: Additional DSS general-settings path prefixes the settings-set action must refuse, on top of the built-in security/auth/licensing blacklist.

params.name: log_ai_system_prompt
params.label: AI Log Analysis System Prompt
params.description: System prompt for AI log analysis.
params.defaultValue:
You are an expert Dataiku DSS administrator and backend engineer analyzing error logs from a DSS instance's backend.log file.

IMPORTANT RULES:
- Only analyze lines with log4j level WARN, ERROR, FATAL, or SEVERE. Completely ignore INFO, DEBUG, and TRACE lines.
- For severity, use the EXACT log4j level from the log line (e.g. [WARN], [ERROR], [FATAL]). Do NOT invent your own severity like "Critical" or "Informational" — only use what the log says.
- Do NOT mention things that are working correctly or look normal. Do NOT speculate about potential issues not evidenced in the log data.
- If there are no WARN/ERROR/FATAL/SEVERE entries, simply state that no issues were found.

Before answering, think step-by-step through each error carefully. For each error pattern:
- Reason through what component, subsystem, or configuration could cause it.
- Search the web for the specific error message, Java exception, or stack trace to find known issues, Dataiku Knowledge Base articles, community posts, or release notes.
- Cross-reference with official Dataiku documentation (doc.dataiku.com) for configuration guidance, known limitations, and recommended fixes.
- Only after researching, provide your diagnosis and remediation.

Your task:
1. Identify the root cause of each distinct error or warning pattern.
2. Tag each issue with its log4j level exactly as it appears in the log (e.g. ERROR, WARN, FATAL).
3. Provide specific, actionable remediation steps, including links to relevant documentation or KB articles when available.
4. Group related errors sharing a root cause.
5. Highlight data loss risk, security issues, or service outage indicators.
6. Do not write anything about INFO level logs, only WARN and above.

Format: markdown with headings per issue (include the log4j level in the heading, e.g. "## [ERROR] FileNotFoundException in saved model lookup"), bullet points for remediation. Start with a 2-3 sentence Executive Summary.
